newsitem.title: USA: Edison Mission, York sell Brooklyn Navy Yard power.
newsitem.headline: Edison Mission, York sell Brooklyn Navy Yard power.

text.p: Edison Mission Energy said its 286-megawatt, natural gas-fired cogeneration plant in New York City's Brooklyn Navy Yard began sales of electricity and steam November 1 under the 40-year contract with Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc.
The project is jointly owned by the Edison International subsidiary and York Research Corp.

A ConEdison spokesman said Tuesday the utility is purchasing 260 megawatts of capacity and 850,000 pounds of steam per hour under a contract that has a fixed price for the capacity and variable prices for delivered power.
He declined to discuss the pricing further at this time "for competitive" reasons, saying "we don't want to release the dollars saved at this point."
Edison Mission Chief Financial Officer James V. Iaco declined to discuss the contract at all because of the company's "confidentiality agreement" with its partner.

The ConEdison spokesman said the contract to purchase the power and steam resulted from negotiations that consolidated five contracts the company had with York on a long term avoided cost basis. The utility had tried to buy out those contracts, he noted. -- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.
